locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_mellin_explicit_formula_round15.md · A fixed smooth witness for which the stated height limit fails
statement: There exists a fixed smooth real f satisfying the pinned manuscript's literal endpoint and local hypotheses whose zero sum fails under symmetric raw-height cutoffs. Disjoint log-coordinate bumps with amplitudes a_j=exp(−(1/2+δ)j), b_j=exp(−(1+δ)j), and separated high-frequency carriers produce symmetric height increments exceeding 2j/5. The arithmetic side has ordinary absolute convergence.
hypotheses: Nontrivial zeta zeros with multiplicity, actual unaveraged cutoffs |Im ρ|≤T, and the auxiliary formula on pinned manuscript pp. 5–6. Uses the unconditional zero count in populated high cells. The compact jump tests in the main theorem have a separate justification.

statement: For h(s)=∫₀∞ f(x)x^(s−1)dx and N_s² the strip area integral of |h(β+it)|²(1+t²)^s, the zero trace is absolutely summable. With r=min(ε/2,1/4), its ℓ¹ bound is C_N/(√π r) times [2·5^s Σ_n log²(2+|n|)/(1+n²)^s]^(1/2) N_s. Restricting the series to |n|>T−1 gives tail O(N_s T^(1/2−s) log(2+T)). The compensated explicit formula follows by compact smooth approximation, with automatic central trace control.
hypotheses: Continuous f with the original endpoint value bounds at margin δ>0, 0<ε<δ, finite norm on β∈[−ε,1+ε], s>1/2. C_N bounds the number of zeta zeros with n≤Im ρ<n+1 by C_N log(2+|n|), including multiplicities.

statement: Replacing the strip weight by w_p(t)=√(1+t²) log^p(e+|t|) gives an absolute zero trace, with tail O(N_log,p [log(2+T)]^((3−p)/2)). Fourier inversion on the central line gives the Dini modulus O(N_log,p [log(e/|u|)]^((1−p)/2)) near u=0. Approximation establishes the same compensated explicit formula.
hypotheses: Continuous f with the original endpoint value bounds, strip margin 0<ε<δ, and finite area norm with p>3. The endpoint claim separately addresses failure of universal absolute sampling at p=3.

statement: For each p>3 a smooth real example lies in the critical-log strip class and in none of the polynomial strip classes with s>1/2. Use disjoint log bumps at j, carrier Γ_j=2^(j²), and amplitudes Γ_j^(−1/2) log^(−p/2)(e+Γ_j) j^(−2)e^(−2j) in x^(−1/2) times the log-coordinate series. Uniform carrier lower bounds give divergence of every heavier polynomial norm.
hypotheses: Fixed ε=1/4 and fixed nonnegative smooth compact bump. The value is O(x^(−2)) as x→∞ and vanishes for x near zero. This example concerns strict class inclusion and has absolute zero trace.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_mellin_explicit_formula_round15.md · A separate finite-cutoff identity and why the main theorem survives
statement: In pinned manuscript p. 8 equation (3.5), the finite-cutoff equality requires the additive gamma-compensator term n∫_(1/ε)^∞ dx/[x(x²−1)] = −(n/2)log(1−ε²). For n=1 and ε=2/3 the missing positive term is (1/2)log(9/5). The term tends to zero at O_n(ε²), and the compact jump formula with midpoint values gives the main limiting identity.
hypotheses: Exact finite equality in the pinned author manuscript, with the manuscript's jump convention. The witness cutoff 3/2 avoids prime powers. This calculation concerns the finite formula and its true limit.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_long_prime_round15.md · An exact limitation of two progression norms
statement: On true supported squarefree four-prime moduli k≈K at P=KT, a nonnegative centered row model satisfies Σ_k max_u|E_(k,u)|≪√(PS) and Σ_(k,u)* |E_(k,u)|²≈PK, where S≈K/log⁴T. Its h=1 real projection with coefficients a_k/k is (12+o(1))√(PS), exceeding T log⁴T by a divergent factor. The common-divisor CRT marginals differ at 1 for two moduli gv₁ and gv₂, excluding a single common unit-supported sequence.
hypotheses: Fixed 1/8<b<1/6, K≈Y^(4b), T≈Y, and all four distinct factors in one fixed near-top multiplicative prime band. This is an abstract implication countermodel; it gives no lower bound for genuine primes.

statement: A sufficient open target on each residual block is Σ_(k≈K,h≈D)|Σ_(p≈P,(p,k)=1)(log p)³p^(−it)[e(−hp/k)−μ(q)/φ(q)]|²≪T^(2−η)K/D with q=k/(h,k), uniformly for |t|≤T^ε and some fixed η>0. Cauchy–Schwarz costs O(T^ε√(D/K)) and the Mellin integral costs O(T^(1−κ)).
hypotheses: T≈Y, DP≈KT, a_k≤24, cutoff H=T^κ with κ sufficiently near one, and 1−κ+ε<η/2 with strict margin. The k-sum may be restricted to actual modulus support. All divisor gcds are retained. No square estimate on genuine primes is claimed.

statement: For the full ordered m-prime coefficient c_m/m! from a finite nonempty set with largest prime p_*, the exact r-way 1-bounded well-factorable level is p_*^(m+r−1). Completely multiplicative |g|≤1 preserves sufficiency and preserves necessity if g(p_*)≠0. For m=4,r=3 the padded Y^(6b) level fits Pascadi's longest-block fixed-residue exponent 5/8 with a strict margin when b<5/28.
hypotheses: Integers m,r≥1, and every prescribed real split Q=∏Q_i with Q_i≥1. The sequence is untruncated. The comparison to Pascadi uses x≈Y^(1+4b) and fixed nonzero residue; no sharp-shell factorability or varying-residue conclusion follows.

statement: Let A_m be the difference between Σ_(n≤x) Λ(n)n^(iδ−1)log^m(x/n) and ∫₁ˣu^(iδ−1)log^m(x/u)du. With L=log x and K=|Im δ|L it is bounded by L^m+4e^K 1_(m=0)+20e^K|iδ−1|L^m+20m e^K L^(m−1). For real |δ|≤1/2 a common bound is 31L^m+20mL^(m−1).
hypotheses: Real x>1, integer m≥0, complex δ; omit the final term for m=0 and take the zeroth log power to be one. The right endpoint includes prime-power jumps. Uses Fiori–Jaskari v2 unconditionally for the absolute PNT error bounds r≤4 and ∫r(u)du/u<20. This is one substitution in Gonek Lemma 8.

statement: A real smooth f vanishing near zero and one and satisfying f(x)=O(x^(−4)) has finite Mellin area norm on β∈[−1/4,5/4] with weight √(1+t²) log³(e+|t|), yet Σ_ρ|h(ρ)| diverges. Every realization of the disjoint finite-carrier packet signs has finite norm, and divergence holds for almost every independent symmetric sign realization.
hypotheses: Actual nontrivial zeta zeros counted with multiplicity, using unconditional Riemann–von Mangoldt counting. The same example excludes universal absolute sampling for p≤3. Signed symmetric height convergence at p=3 remains open.

statement: The printed E_h=(P+Q)/2−i(P−Q)/(2h), where P(z)=ξ(1/2−iz+h) and Q(z)=ξ(1/2−iz−h), equals its Schwarz reflection for every real h≠0 because P#=Q and Q#=P. Thus h=1/2,z=i already gives equality in the absolute values required to be strictly ordered by (5.1). The local limit of the printed family is ξ−iξ′.
hypotheses: The display immediately preceding (5.5) in the pinned arXiv v6 and journal versions. The separately defined h=0 function and the fixed-boundary spectral results are outside this claim.

locator: audits/adversarial_reviews/director_morse_scoped_round15.md · The explicit quotient has the opposite Herglotz sign
statement: At z=i and x=e^u, the printed quotient (6.2) is −i exp(−x)/(1+x), so u=0 gives −i/(2e). Its imaginary part is strictly negative. With the printed decomposition E=A−iB, the compatible Herglotz quotient is +B/A.
hypotheses: Equation (6.2) and the positive-imaginary convention in the pinned arXiv v6 and journal versions. This is an auxiliary quotient in the z variable. The Appendix B Weyl–Titchmarsh quotient uses energy E=z² and has its own sign.
